Best Actor Oscar winners, by year of the.Clark Gable: Gable won for It Happened One Night, a screwball comedy that swept the big five Oscars. He famously played the rogue in Gone with the Wind years later.
Best Actor Oscar winners, by year of the.Humphrey Bogart: Bogart won for The African Queen, playing a gruff riverboat captain opposite Katharine Hepburn, after years of tough-guy supporting roles.
Best Actor Oscar winners, by year of the.Marlon Brando (first win): Brando won for On the Waterfront in 1954, and later famously refused his second Oscar for The Godfather as a protest.
Best Actor Oscar winners, by year of the.Jack Nicholson (first win): Nicholson won for One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest, in which he played a rebellious patient in a mental hospital.
Best Actor Oscar winners, by year of the.Tom Hanks (first win): Hanks won consecutive Best Actor Oscars, first for Philadelphia and then for Forrest Gump, a rare back-to-back achievement.
Best Actor Oscar winners, by year of the.Russell Crowe: Crowe won for Gladiator, playing the Roman general Maximus, and the film also took Best Picture that year.
Best Actor Oscar winners, by year of the.Jamie Foxx: Foxx won for playing Ray Charles in Ray, and he performed many of the musical sequences himself, playing the piano.
Best Actor Oscar winners, by year of the.Daniel Day-Lewis (Lincoln): Day-Lewis became the first actor to win three Best Actor Oscars, and Lincoln gave him that record-setting third statue.
Best Actor Oscar winners, by year of the.Leonardo DiCaprio: DiCaprio finally won for The Revenant after years of nominations, a role famous for its brutal cold and a gruelling shoot.
Best Actor Oscar winners, by year of the.Cillian Murphy: Murphy won for Oppenheimer, playing the father of the atomic bomb, after a long career that began with Irish stage and films like 28 Days Later.

Tree climbers by weight.Red-eyed tree frog: By day it sleeps with green skin and closed eyes, and when disturbed flashes red eyes and orange feet to startle predators.
Tree climbers by weight.Pygmy marmoset: The world's smallest monkey gouges holes in tree bark with its teeth and eats the sap that flows out.
Tree climbers by weight.Red squirrel: It buries thousands of nuts and forgets many, planting new trees. In Britain, grey squirrels have pushed reds to the edge.
Tree climbers by weight.Squirrel monkey: Its brain is proportionally one of the biggest of any primate, and troops of dozens travel through the canopy together.
Tree climbers by weight.Green tree python: Hatchlings are bright yellow or red and turn green as they grow, and adults rest coiled over a branch.
Tree climbers by weight.Three-toed sloth: Sloths come down to the ground only about once a week to defecate, and algae grows in their fur.
Tree climbers by weight.Koala: Eucalyptus leaves give little energy, so koalas sleep up to 18 hours a day, and their fingerprints look remarkably human.
Tree climbers by weight.Clouded leopard: Its canine teeth are the longest relative to body size of any living cat, and it can hang upside down from branches.
Tree climbers by weight.Chimpanzee: Chimps build a fresh sleeping nest in the trees every night, bending branches into a platform.
Tree climbers by weight.Orangutan (male): The largest tree-dwelling mammal. Its name means 'person of the forest' in Malay.

Studio Ghibli films by release.Castle in the Sky: Studio Ghibli's first film as a studio; Joe Hisaishi composed the score.
Studio Ghibli films by release.My Neighbor Totoro: Totoro, the film's fluffy forest spirit, is Ghibli's mascot and appears in its logo.
Studio Ghibli films by release.Kiki's Delivery Service: Based on Eiko Kadono's novel, it follows a young witch who delivers goods by broom.
Studio Ghibli films by release.Porco Rosso: The hero is a pig-faced World War I pilot in the Adriatic.
Studio Ghibli films by release.Princess Mononoke: It became Japan's highest-grossing film at the time.
Studio Ghibli films by release.Spirited Away: It won the Oscar for Best Animated Feature in 2003, a hand-drawn Japanese first.
Studio Ghibli films by release.Howl's Moving Castle: Based on Diana Wynne Jones's novel, it features a walking castle and a young woman cursed with old age.
Studio Ghibli films by release.Ponyo: Inspired by The Little Mermaid, it was drawn with hand-painted waves.
Studio Ghibli films by release.The Wind Rises: Miyazaki said it would be his last film; it is about Jiro Horikoshi, designer of the Zero fighter.
Studio Ghibli films by release.The Boy and the Heron: It won the 2024 Oscar for Best Animated Feature, and Miyazaki came out of retirement for it.

When these London bridges opened.Westminster Bridge (current): Painted green like the House of Commons benches, it inspired Wordsworth's famous sonnet.
When these London bridges opened.Blackfriars Bridge (current): Queen Victoria opened this bridge in 1869, near the site of a Dominican priory, the Black Friars.
When these London bridges opened.Albert Bridge: Nicknamed the Trembling Lady, soldiers are told to break step when crossing it.
When these London bridges opened.Hammersmith Bridge: Bombed by the IRA, it was closed to traffic in 2019 because of cracks.
When these London bridges opened.Tower Bridge: It is often mistaken for London Bridge, and its bascules lift for ships.
When these London bridges opened.Southwark Bridge (current): Rebuilt in steel; its predecessor by John Rennie was a cast-iron arch bridge.
When these London bridges opened.Chelsea Bridge (current): A suspension bridge near Battersea Power Station, it replaced an 1858 bridge.
When these London bridges opened.Waterloo Bridge (current): Called the Ladies' Bridge because women workers largely built it during World War II.
When these London bridges opened.London Bridge (current): The previous bridge, from 1831, was sold to the US and rebuilt at Lake Havasu City, Arizona.
When these London bridges opened.Millennium Bridge: Nicknamed the Wobbly Bridge, it swayed on opening and closed for two years.

How much these storage media can hold.Punch card: The standard IBM card has 80 columns, and the width became a standard for early computer terminals and text displays.
How much these storage media can hold.5.25-inch floppy (DD): It replaced the 8-inch floppy and stored 360 KB, which was enough for a program and its data on early PCs.
How much these storage media can hold.3.5-inch floppy (HD): Its hard case and 1.44 MB capacity made it the standard for years, and its image lives on as the save icon.
How much these storage media can hold.IBM 350 RAMAC hard drive: It filled a closet with 50 spinning disks the size of large pizzas, and was leased by IBM in 1956 for thousands of dollars monthly.
How much these storage media can hold.Iomega Zip disk: These disks were once a rival to floppies, but were infamous for failing in a way called the 'click of death'.
How much these storage media can hold.CD-ROM: Legend ties the original 74-minute length to Beethoven's Ninth Symphony, so it would fit on one disc.
How much these storage media can hold.DVD (single layer): It stands for digital versatile disc, and a dual-layer version holds about 8.5 GB.
How much these storage media can hold.HD DVD (single layer): It lost the format war with Blu-ray in 2008, after Warner and other studios dropped it.
How much these storage media can hold.Blu-ray (single layer): A blue-violet laser with a shorter wavelength lets Blu-ray pack data much tighter than a DVD.
How much these storage media can hold.SDXC card (max spec): The spec allows up to 2 terabytes in a card the size of a fingernail, though real cards of that size are rare.

When Harry Met Sally... is famous for its deli scene, and Nora Ephron's script asks whether men and women can be friends.
Romantic comedies by release.Pretty Woman: Pretty Woman made Julia Roberts a star, and the film has the famously touching scene of a shopping trip on Rodeo Drive.
Romantic comedies by release.Sleepless in Seattle: Sleepless in Seattle was inspired by An Affair to Remember, and the lovers famously don't meet until the very end.
Romantic comedies by release.Four Weddings and a Funeral: Four Weddings and a Funeral was a huge British hit, and its funeral scene featured a reading of Auden's poem.
Romantic comedies by release.Clueless: Clueless was a modern retelling of Jane Austen's Emma, set in a Beverly Hills high school.
Romantic comedies by release.Notting Hill: Notting Hill was written by Richard Curtis and sets a bookshop owner against a famous actress, and the bookshop was a real shop.
Romantic comedies by release.Bridget Jones's Diary: Bridget Jones's Diary was based on Helen Fielding's novel, which itself was loosely inspired by Pride and Prejudice.
Romantic comedies by release.Love Actually: Love Actually has ten interwoven stories set in the weeks before Christmas, and it has become a holiday tradition.
Romantic comedies by release.The Proposal: The Proposal starred Sandra Bullock and Ryan Reynolds, and it was a big hit set in Alaska.
Romantic comedies by release.Crazy Rich Asians: Crazy Rich Asians was the first major Hollywood film in over 25 years with a majority Asian cast, and it was a hit.

Small papers and cards by area.A10 sheet: Every A size is exactly half of the one before, and an A0 sheet has an area of one square meter.
Small papers and cards by area.A9 sheet: Fold an A4 sheet in half five times and you'll arrive at this size.
Small papers and cards by area.A8 sheet: Sixteen of them would cover a single A4 sheet.
Small papers and cards by area.Credit card: It uses the same standard size as bank cards and many driver's licenses, the ISO ID-1 format.
Small papers and cards by area.Poker playing card: This is the standard size for poker, 2.5 by 3.5 inches, while bridge cards are a little narrower.
Small papers and cards by area.A7 sheet: Four of these make up an A5 sheet, and this size is typical of small notepads.
Small papers and cards by area.US banknote: The US has kept all bills at one size since 1929, so a one-dollar note and a hundred are the same.
Small papers and cards by area.A6 sheet: It is a very common postcard size around the world.
Small papers and cards by area.A5 sheet: Half of A4, it's a standard notebook size, and a favorite for planners.
Small papers and cards by area.A4 sheet: Almost every country uses it as the standard, apart from the United States and Canada, which use letter size.

When these psychological effects were de.Halo effect: Edward Thorndike found that officers rated as handsome were also judged better at everything else, the bias he called the halo effect.
When these psychological effects were de.Zeigarnik effect: Bluma Zeigarnik noticed that waiters remembered unpaid orders better than settled ones, showing unfinished tasks stick in the mind.
When these psychological effects were de.Stroop effect: Naming the ink colour of the word red printed in blue is slow because reading is automatic; try it.
When these psychological effects were de.Barnum (Forer) effect: Forer gave students identical personal profiles and they rated them highly accurate, which explains why horoscopes feel personal.
When these psychological effects were de.The powerful placebo: Henry Beecher's paper showed about a third of patients improved on inert treatments, spurring controlled trials.
When these psychological effects were de.Learned helplessness: Martin Seligman found dogs that could not escape shocks later stopped trying even when escape was easy.
When these psychological effects were de.Flynn effect: James Flynn documented that average IQ test scores rose about three points per decade through the 20th century.
When these psychological effects were de.Baader-Meinhof phenomenon: Named by a newspaper commenter after a German militant group, it is the illusion that something you just noticed is suddenly everywhere.
When these psychological effects were de.Spotlight effect: When people wore an embarrassing T-shirt, they hugely overestimated how many others noticed; most are thinking of themselves.
When these psychological effects were de.Mandela effect: Fiona Broome named it after many people falsely recalled Nelson Mandela dying in prison in the 1980s; he died in 2013.

Anglo-Saxon and Danish kings, by start o.Alfred the Great: Alfred defended Wessex against Viking invasion and is the only English monarch to be called 'the Great', partly for promoting learning and law in English.
Anglo-Saxon and Danish kings, by start o.Edward the Elder: Alfred's son began reconquering Danish-held England, working with his sister Aethelflaed, the Lady of the Mercians, who led armies of her own.
Anglo-Saxon and Danish kings, by start o.Aethelstan: Often called the first king of all England, he took York in 927 and won a huge victory over a Scots-Viking alliance at Brunanburh in 937.
Anglo-Saxon and Danish kings, by start o.Edmund I: Aethelstan's half-brother took the throne at about 18 and was murdered at a feast in 946, reportedly stabbed while defending his steward.
Anglo-Saxon and Danish kings, by start o.Edgar the Peaceful: His nickname came from a time of relative calm, and his coronation at Bath in 973 set a pattern still echoed in royal ceremonies today.
Anglo-Saxon and Danish kings, by start o.Aethelred the Unready: His nickname comes from Old English 'unraed', meaning ill-advised, a pun on his name Aethelred, 'noble counsel'. He faced renewed Viking attacks.
Anglo-Saxon and Danish kings, by start o.Cnut the Great: A Dane who conquered England, he also ruled Denmark and Norway. Legend says he vainly ordered the tide to stop, to show kings have limits.
Anglo-Saxon and Danish kings, by start o.Harthacnut: Cnut's son ruled England for only two years and died, reportedly while drinking at a wedding feast, ending the Danish royal line.
Anglo-Saxon and Danish kings, by start o.Edward the Confessor: He founded Westminster Abbey and spent years in exile in Normandy; his childless death in 1066 set off the succession crisis behind the Norman Conquest.
Anglo-Saxon and Danish kings, by start o.Harold Godwinson: England's last Anglo-Saxon king reigned only about nine months in 1066, beating Norwegians at Stamford Bridge before falling to William at Hastings.

Blizzards and winter storms, in order.Great Blizzard, US Northeast: The Great Blizzard of 1888 buried the Northeast under up to 50 inches of snow and led New York to put its subways and wires underground.
Blizzards and winter storms, in order.Great Lakes White Hurricane: The 1913 Great Lakes Storm sank a dozen ships and killed about 250 sailors, with winds hurricane-strength.
Blizzards and winter storms, in order.Knickerbocker Storm: The Knickerbocker Storm collapsed the roof of Washington's Knickerbocker Theatre under snow, and it killed 98.
Blizzards and winter storms, in order.Armistice Day Blizzard: The Armistice Day Blizzard hit the Midwest on a mild morning and caught duck hunters, killing about 150 people.
Blizzards and winter storms, in order.Iran blizzard: The 1972 blizzard in Iran is the deadliest ever recorded, killing around 4,000 after as much as 8 feet of snow.
Blizzards and winter storms, in order.New England blizzard: The 1978 blizzard in New England paralyzed the region for days, and stranded thousands of cars on highways.
Blizzards and winter storms, in order.Storm of the Century (US): The Storm of the Century in 1993 hit much of the eastern US, and spread from Cuba to Canada.
Blizzards and winter storms, in order.Snowmageddon (US): 'Snowmageddon' shut down Washington D.C. with record snowfall, and it was nicknamed by President Obama.
Blizzards and winter storms, in order.Texas winter storm Uri: Winter Storm Uri caused huge power failures in Texas, and the grid came within minutes of a long collapse.
Blizzards and winter storms, in order.Buffalo Christmas blizzard: The Buffalo storm lasted several days over Christmas, and its snow was fed by the lake and buried cars and homes.

Moons and worlds, by when they were disc.Jupiter's four big moons: Galileo's telescope showed Io, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto circling Jupiter, proof that not everything orbits Earth.
Moons and worlds, by when they were disc.Titan: Christiaan Huygens found Saturn's largest moon, which has thick nitrogen air and methane lakes; a probe named for him landed there in 2005.
Moons and worlds, by when they were disc.Uranus: William Herschel first thought he had found a comet; it was the first planet discovered with a telescope.
Moons and worlds, by when they were disc.Ceres: Giuseppe Piazzi found it, first called a planet, then an asteroid, and since 2006 it has been a dwarf planet, the only one in the inner solar system.
Moons and worlds, by when they were disc.Neptune: Le Verrier predicted its position from Uranus's odd orbit, and Galle found it in Berlin on the first night of searching.
Moons and worlds, by when they were disc.Phobos and Deimos: Asaph Hall found Mars's two small moons; Phobos is spiraling inward and may break apart in tens of millions of years.
Moons and worlds, by when they were disc.Pluto: Clyde Tombaugh, a young Kansas astronomer, found it; its name was suggested by 11-year-old Venetia Burney, and it lost planet status in 2006.
Moons and worlds, by when they were disc.Miranda: This moon of Uranus has enormous cliffs and a patchwork surface, as if it had been broken apart and reassembled.
Moons and worlds, by when they were disc.Charon: James Christy found it; Charon is so large relative to Pluto that the two orbit a point in space between them.
Moons and worlds, by when they were disc.Eris: About as wide as Pluto but more massive, its discovery led to the 2006 redefinition of planets that demoted Pluto.

Turning points in Chinese history.Qing take Beijing: Manchu forces entered the capital after rebels toppled the Ming, founding a dynasty that ruled China until 1912.
Turning points in Chinese history.First Opium War: Britain went to war to protect its opium sales into China; the 1842 Treaty of Nanking handed Hong Kong Island to Britain.
Turning points in Chinese history.Taiping Rebellion: Led by Hong Xiuquan, who claimed to be Jesus's younger brother, this civil war killed an estimated 20 million people or more.
Turning points in Chinese history.Boxer Rebellion: Rebels from a martial-arts movement, called Boxers by foreigners, attacked missionaries and besieged the Beijing legations for 55 days.
Turning points in Chinese history.Xinhai Revolution: The uprising began in Wuchang in October and ended over 2,000 years of imperial rule, with Sun Yat-sen as provisional president.
Turning points in Chinese history.The Long March: Communist forces retreated thousands of kilometers across mountains and rivers, and Mao Zedong emerged as the party's leader along the way.
Turning points in Chinese history.People's Republic founded: Mao proclaimed it from Tiananmen Gate on October 1, while the defeated Nationalists retreated to the island of Taiwan.
Turning points in Chinese history.Cultural Revolution: Mao launched it to purge supposed enemies, with schools closed and Red Guards mobilized; its upheaval lasted about a decade.
Turning points in Chinese history.Tiananmen Square protests: Student-led demonstrations calling for reform filled the square for weeks before the army cleared it in early June.
Turning points in Chinese history.Hong Kong handover: Britain returned Hong Kong at midnight on July 1 under 'one country, two systems', ending over 150 years of colonial rule.

First satellite launched on a nation's o.Soviet Union: Sputnik 1, a beeping metal sphere about 58 cm wide, kicked off the Space Race.
First satellite launched on a nation's o.United States: Its Explorer 1 discovered Earth's radiation belts, now named after James Van Allen.
First satellite launched on a nation's o.France: Astérix launched on a Diamant rocket from Algeria, making France the third nation in space.
First satellite launched on a nation's o.Japan: Ohsumi flew after four failed attempts, on a Lambda 4S rocket.
First satellite launched on a nation's o.United Kingdom: Prospero flew on a Black Arrow rocket from Woomera in Australia, and Britain then dropped its launcher program.
First satellite launched on a nation's o.India: Rohini rode the SLV-3 rocket, developed by ISRO under project director A. P. J. Abdul Kalam.
First satellite launched on a nation's o.Israel: Ofek-1 launched on a Shavit rocket, and Israel launches west over the Mediterranean to avoid its neighbors.
First satellite launched on a nation's o.Iran: The Omid satellite launched on a Safir rocket in February 2009.
First satellite launched on a nation's o.North Korea: Kwangmyongsong-3 Unit 2 reached orbit in December 2012 after an earlier failed attempt.
First satellite launched on a nation's o.South Korea: The Nuri rocket's second flight in June 2022 placed satellites in orbit, making it the seventh nation.

When these word games appeared.The crossword puzzle: Arthur Wynne published the first one in the New York World in December 1913, shaped like a diamond.
When these word games appeared.Scrabble (under that name): Alfred Butts invented it in the 1930s under another name, and James Brunot later renamed it and sold it.
When these word games appeared.Mad Libs: The game's name is a pun on libs, and it began as a pad of fill-in-the-blank stories created by Roger Price and Leonard Stern.
When these word games appeared.Boggle: This game sets a plastic grid of letter cubes shaking, and players have three minutes to find words.
When these word games appeared.Upwords: Words stack on top of one another in this 3D take on Scrabble, so a tall tower of tiles can earn extra points.
When these word games appeared.Bananagrams: This tile-peeling race has no board, and its name is a play on being driven bananas.
When these word games appeared.Words With Friends: This online game lets friends play asynchronously, and it was a huge hit on Facebook around 2009.
When these word games appeared.Wordle: Josh Wardle made it as a gift for his partner, and the New York Times bought it in 2022 for a price in the low seven figures.
When these word games appeared.Quordle: This game asks you to solve four Wordle-style puzzles at once, with nine guesses to find all four answers.
When these word games appeared.NYT Connections: The New York Times puzzle asks you to sort 16 words into four hidden groups, and its trickiest groups use words that overlap.

Milligrams in a standard dose (US).Folic acid tablet: Folic acid taken before pregnancy helps reduce the risk of neural tube defects in babies.
Milligrams in a standard dose (US).Claritin tablet: This allergy tablet is a once-a-day antihistamine, and it was made popular as non-drowsy.
Milligrams in a standard dose (US).Benadryl tablet: This antihistamine works for allergies, but its drowsy effect is why it also appears in sleep aids.
Milligrams in a standard dose (US).Low-dose aspirin: Doctors recommend this low-dose aspirin for some patients to help prevent heart attacks, and it's often called baby aspirin.
Milligrams in a standard dose (US).Advil tablet: Ibuprofen is an anti-inflammatory, and a common over-the-counter tablet contains this dose.
Milligrams in a standard dose (US).Regular aspirin: A regular aspirin tablet contains 325 mg, and it was first made by Bayer in 1899.
Milligrams in a standard dose (US).Extra Strength Tylenol: Acetaminophen is called paracetamol in much of the world, and it's the common painkiller in Tylenol.
Milligrams in a standard dose (US).Vitamin C tablet: One tablet delivers a gram of vitamin C, and humans, unlike most animals, can't make it themselves.
Milligrams in a standard dose (US).Daily max OTC ibuprofen: This is the daily ceiling for over-the-counter ibuprofen without a doctor's advice, and higher doses raise stomach and kidney risks.
Milligrams in a standard dose (US).Daily max acetaminophen: This maximum daily dose of acetaminophen is the limit for adults, and exceeding it can damage the liver.

Speeds in physics, from sound to light.Sound in air: Sound travels about a kilometer in three seconds, and that's why thunder lags behind lightning.
Speeds in physics, from sound to light.Earth's spin at the equator: The five Panthera big cats are lion, tiger, leopard, jaguar and snow leopard, and the snow leopard is the one that can't roar.
Speeds in physics, from sound to light.Moon orbiting Earth: The Moon moves at about a kilometer per second as it orbits us, and it drifts away by a few centimeters a year.
Speeds in physics, from sound to light.Sound in water: Sound travels faster in water than in air, which is why whales can communicate across long distances.
Speeds in physics, from sound to light.Earth's escape velocity: This is the speed a rocket needs to break away from Earth's gravity without further propulsion.
Speeds in physics, from sound to light.Voyager 1 cruising: Voyager 1 is the farthest human-made object, and it is speeding out of the solar system.
Speeds in physics, from sound to light.Earth orbiting the Sun: Earth orbits the Sun at about 30 km/s, or around 107,000 km/h.
Speeds in physics, from sound to light.Parker Solar Probe at peak: The spacecraft is the fastest human-made object, set to reach this speed in the Sun's gravity.
Speeds in physics, from sound to light.Sun orbiting the galaxy: Our Sun moves at about 230 km/s around the Milky Way's center, taking about 230 million years to circle.
Speeds in physics, from sound to light.Light in vacuum: Light travels at a speed that nothing with mass can match, and it takes about eight minutes to reach us from the Sun.

Weird and wonderful animals by weight.Naked mole-rat: It lives over 30 years and rarely gets cancer, and colonies are ruled by a queen like bees.
Weird and wonderful animals by weight.Pink fairy armadillo: The smallest armadillo, from Argentina, burrows, and its shell is attached only along its back.
Weird and wonderful animals by weight.Hoatzin: This South American bird ferments leaves in its crop like a cow, so it smells bad; chicks have wing claws.
Weird and wonderful animals by weight.Aye-aye: This Madagascar lemur taps wood and fishes out grubs with an extra-long middle finger.
Weird and wonderful animals by weight.Shoebill: This Africa bird has a bill like a shoe and stands motionless for hours, waiting for fish.
Weird and wonderful animals by weight.Tasmanian devil: It has the strongest bite for its size of any living mammal.
Weird and wonderful animals by weight.Giant pangolin: Its scales are made of keratin, like fingernails, and pangolins are among the most trafficked mammals.
Weird and wonderful animals by weight.Aardvark: Its name means 'earth pig' in Afrikaans, though it is not related to pigs; it eats termites and ants.
Weird and wonderful animals by weight.Okapi: Zebra-striped legs, but a relative of the giraffe; science did not know it until 1901.
Weird and wonderful animals by weight.Dugong: A relative of the elephant, called a sea cow, it may have inspired sailors' mermaid legends.

Launch price in the US.Game Boy: Nintendo's 1989 handheld came with Tetris, and its dim green screen did not stop it from selling over 100 million units with its successor.
Launch price in the US.PlayStation: At a 1995 trade show a Sony executive said just '299 dollars' and left the stage, undercutting Sega's rival Saturn by 100 dollars.
Launch price in the US.Apple Watch (Sport, 38mm): The 2015 launch spanned from this entry model to a gold Edition costing 10,000 dollars or more.
Launch price in the US.Original iPod: Apple's 2001 pitch was '1,000 songs in your pocket', and the first model worked only with Macs.
Launch price in the US.Original iPhone (4GB): Two months after launch Apple cut the price of its 8GB model by 200 dollars, angering early buyers, who were then offered a 100 dollar credit.
Launch price in the US.Commodore 64: Launched in 1982, it is widely considered the best-selling single computer model ever, with well over ten million sold.
Launch price in the US.Apple I: Wozniak's hand-built board had no case, keyboard or monitor. Its odd price reportedly came from his liking for repeating digits.
Launch price in the US.IBM PC: Its open design, with an Intel chip and Microsoft's DOS, let rival makers copy it and shaped the PC industry for decades.
Launch price in the US.Macintosh 128K: It was introduced in 1984 with a Super Bowl ad directed by Ridley Scott, and its price included a mouse.
Launch price in the US.Apple Lisa: The 1983 Lisa had a graphical interface but flopped, and Apple reportedly buried thousands of unsold units in a Utah landfill.

Marvel Cinematic Universe films by relea.Iron Man: Robert Downey Jr. was a risky casting choice, and the film's success launched a huge shared universe that now spans dozens of films.
Marvel Cinematic Universe films by relea.Thor: The god of thunder was played by Chris Hemsworth, an unknown Australian actor, and Kenneth Branagh directed.
Marvel Cinematic Universe films by relea.The Avengers: The team-up film brought together the first heroes, and it was the first Marvel film to gross over a billion dollars.
Marvel Cinematic Universe films by relea.Guardians of the Galaxy: This film made a talking raccoon and tree beloved, and it used 1970s songs on a mixtape, which became a hit.
Marvel Cinematic Universe films by relea.Ant-Man: The hero who shrinks was originally to be directed by Edgar Wright, and the film is the first film to use the Quantum Realm.
Marvel Cinematic Universe films by relea.Doctor Strange: This film features Benedict Cumberbatch as a surgeon who becomes a sorcerer, and it has astonishing city-bending visuals.
Marvel Cinematic Universe films by relea.Black Panther: This film was the first superhero film nominated for the Best Picture Oscar, and it is set in Wakanda.
Marvel Cinematic Universe films by relea.Avengers: Endgame: This film wrapped up the Infinity Saga, and it became the highest-grossing film at the time, passing Avatar.
Marvel Cinematic Universe films by relea.Shang-Chi: The film features Simu Liu as the first Asian lead in the franchise, and it combines kung fu with mythology.
Marvel Cinematic Universe films by relea.Deadpool & Wolverine: The film paired two popular characters, and it was the first R-rated MCU film, and it grossed over a billion dollars.

Statues and sculptures, by height.Manneken Pis: Brussels' tiny fountain boy has a wardrobe of over 1,000 costumes that he is dressed in on special days.
Statues and sculptures, by height.The Little Mermaid statue: Based on Andersen's tale and looking over Copenhagen harbor, her head has been stolen and sawn off more than once.
Statues and sculptures, by height.Venus de Milo: Found on the Greek island of Milos in 1820, her missing arms have fueled debate for two centuries. She is in the Louvre.
Statues and sculptures, by height.Michelangelo's David: Michelangelo carved him in his twenties from a single marble block that other sculptors had abandoned.
Statues and sculptures, by height.Angel of the North: Antony Gormley's steel figure near Gateshead has wings 54 m across, wider than a jumbo jet's.
Statues and sculptures, by height.Christ the Redeemer: Finished in 1931 and covered in soapstone tiles, this Rio landmark is often struck by lightning.
Statues and sculptures, by height.Statue of Liberty: A gift from France, it was shipped in pieces, and its green color is copper oxidizing.
Statues and sculptures, by height.The Motherland Calls: Honoring the Battle of Stalingrad in Volgograd, the 85 m figure includes a 33 m sword.
Statues and sculptures, by height.Spring Temple Buddha: On top of its pedestal and lotus throne, the whole monument in Henan, China reaches about 208 m.
Statues and sculptures, by height.Statue of Unity: India's tribute to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, in Gujarat, is the tallest statue in the world.

Organs and body parts by typical adult w.Stapes (ear bone): The stirrup is the smallest bone in the body, about 3 mm long, and passes vibrations into the inner ear.
Organs and body parts by typical adult w.Pineal gland: Descartes called this pea-sized gland the seat of the soul. It actually makes the sleep hormone melatonin.
Organs and body parts by typical adult w.Pituitary gland: This pea-sized gland at the brain's base is the master gland, directing many of the body's other hormone glands.
Organs and body parts by typical adult w.One eyeball: Eyes are already about two thirds of adult size at birth, unlike most other body parts.
Organs and body parts by typical adult w.Thyroid gland: This butterfly-shaped neck gland controls metabolism and needs iodine, which is why table salt is often iodized.
Organs and body parts by typical adult w.Pancreas: It is both digestive and hormonal, making enzymes for digestion and insulin for blood sugar.
Organs and body parts by typical adult w.Spleen: It filters blood and recycles old red cells, but you can live without it.
Organs and body parts by typical adult w.Heart: About the size of a fist, it pumps thousands of liters of blood every day.
Organs and body parts by typical adult w.Liver: The heaviest internal organ, it can regrow after part of it is removed.
Organs and body parts by typical adult w.Skin: The largest organ covers about 2 sq m and renews itself roughly every month.

Superhero TV series premieres.Adventures of Superman: Starring George Reeves, it ran six seasons and made flying Superman a household figure.
Superhero TV series premieres.Batman (Adam West): Camp, with onscreen 'POW!' fight captions, it was a smash hit but cancelled after three seasons.
Superhero TV series premieres.Wonder Woman: Lynda Carter starred in it, and the spinning transformation became its signature.
Superhero TV series premieres.The Incredible Hulk: Bill Bixby and Lou Ferrigno starred, and its sad piano theme, The Lonely Man, ended each episode.
Superhero TV series premieres.Lois & Clark: It focused on the Daily Planet romance, with Dean Cain as Clark, and ran four seasons.
Superhero TV series premieres.Smallville: One of the longest-running superhero series ever, it followed Clark Kent's early years in Kansas.
Superhero TV series premieres.Arrow: It launched the Arrowverse, a set of interconnected superhero shows on the CW.
Superhero TV series premieres.Daredevil (Netflix): Charlie Cox starred, and it is famed for a hallway fight filmed in one long take.
Superhero TV series premieres.The Boys: Based on a Garth Ennis comic, it satirizes superheroes as corporate celebrities.
Superhero TV series premieres.WandaVision: Marvel Studios' first Disney+ series mimicked decades of sitcom styles.

When these childhood classics first appe.Teddy bear: It is named for Theodore Roosevelt, after he refused to shoot a tethered bear on a 1902 hunting trip.
When these childhood classics first appe.Crayola crayons: The name blends craie, French for chalk, with ola, from oily, and the first box held eight colors.
When these childhood classics first appe.Lincoln Logs: Invented by John Lloyd Wright, son of Frank Lloyd Wright, inspired by his father's earthquake-proof Tokyo hotel.
When these childhood classics first appe.View-Master: Stereoscopic reels of 3D pictures were widely used by the military for training in World War II.
When these childhood classics first appe.Silly Putty: Discovered accidentally in efforts to make synthetic rubber in WWII, it can copy newsprint.
When these childhood classics first appe.Matchbox cars: The toy cars were sold in matchbox-sized cases, after Jack Odell made one for his daughter.
When these childhood classics first appe.LEGO brick: The name comes from Danish leg godt, meaning play well, and a 1958 patent gave bricks their stud-and-tube grip.
When these childhood classics first appe.Lite-Brite: A bulb behind black paper lights up colored pegs pushed through it.
When these childhood classics first appe.Speak and Spell: Texas Instruments' talking toy was one of the first to use a single speech-synthesis chip, and it appeared in E.T.
When these childhood classics first appe.Transformers: The toys were repackaged by Hasbro from Japanese lines called Diaclone and Micro Change.

Birth years of these music legends.Chuck Berry: His duck walk and guitar riffs shaped rock and roll, and Johnny B. Goode was sent into space on Voyager's Golden Record.
Birth years of these music legends.Elvis Presley: Born in Tupelo, Mississippi, he sold over a billion records worldwide.
Birth years of these music legends.Bob Dylan: Born Robert Zimmerman, he won the 2016 Nobel Prize in Literature for new poetic expressions in the American song tradition.
Birth years of these music legends.Freddie Mercury: He was born Farrokh Bulsara in Zanzibar, and the Queen frontman's range spanned about four octaves.
Birth years of these music legends.Bruce Springsteen: His nickname is The Boss, which reportedly started when he handed out the band's pay.
Birth years of these music legends.Prince: He played all the instruments on his first album, For You, and he was born in Minneapolis.
Birth years of these music legends.Kurt Cobain: His band's Nevermind knocked Michael Jackson's Dangerous off the number one spot in 1992.
Birth years of these music legends.Beyoncé: She has won more Grammy awards than any other artist, and she started in Destiny's Child.
Birth years of these music legends.Taylor Swift: She is re-recording her early albums as Taylor's Version to own her masters.
Birth years of these music legends.Billie Eilish: In 2020 she became the youngest artist to win all four main Grammy categories in one night, at 18.

Roman numerals, from smallest to largest.IX: Writing nine as IX, one before ten, is subtractive notation; early Romans often wrote VIIII, and some clock faces still show IIII for four.
Roman numerals, from smallest to largest.XIV: Louis XIV of France, the Sun King, reigned 72 years, one of the longest reigns of any monarch in European history.
Roman numerals, from smallest to largest.XXXVIII: It takes seven symbols to write 38, because Roman numerals have no zero or place value and repeat letters up to three times.
Roman numerals, from smallest to largest.XLIX: Purists write 49 as XLIX (forty, then nine), not IL; the standard rule lets I, X and C be subtracted only from the next two larger symbols.
Roman numerals, from smallest to largest.LXXXVIII: LXXXVIII, with eight symbols, is the longest numeral you can write below 100, which is a good reason Romans never did long sums on paper.
Roman numerals, from smallest to largest.XC: XC is 100 minus 10. The C comes from centum, Latin for hundred, which also gives us the words century and percent.
Roman numerals, from smallest to largest.CDXLIV: CDXLIV uses subtraction three times (CD, XL, IV), so 444 takes six symbols instead of the twelve the purely additive method would need.
Roman numerals, from smallest to largest.DCCC: Charlemagne was crowned emperor by the pope in Rome on Christmas Day of this year, 800, reviving the idea of an emperor in the West.
Roman numerals, from smallest to largest.MCDXCII: In 1492 Columbus reached the Caribbean, and in the same year Granada fell, ending Muslim rule in Spain after nearly eight centuries.
Roman numerals, from smallest to largest.MMXX: MMXX is 2020, a year many remember for the pandemic; Romans never numbered years like this, since they counted from the founding of Rome.

Backyard and garden critters by weight.Black garden ant: Ants can carry many times their own weight, and some Lasius niger queens live more than two decades, among the longest-lived insects.
Backyard and garden critters by weight.Honeybee: A honeybee makes only about a twelfth of a teaspoon of honey in her whole life, so a jar takes thousands of bee lifetimes.
Backyard and garden critters by weight.Bumblebee queen: Only bumblebee queens survive winter, hibernating alone underground, then founding a whole new colony by themselves in spring.
Backyard and garden critters by weight.European robin: Robins defend their territories fiercely, and in towns some sing at night beneath streetlights.
Backyard and garden critters by weight.Common toad: Toads crawl rather than hop, and each spring many return to the pond where they were born, even crossing busy roads.
Backyard and garden critters by weight.Magpie: Magpies can recognize themselves in a mirror, a mark of intelligence few animals show, though studies suggest they don't favor shiny things.
Backyard and garden critters by weight.Gray squirrel: Gray squirrels bury thousands of nuts each autumn and forget many, which helps plant new oak trees; they fake-bury when watched.
Backyard and garden critters by weight.European hedgehog: A hedgehog has several thousand spines, can roll into a tight ball, and hibernates through winter in a nest of leaves.
Backyard and garden critters by weight.Red fox: Foxes may use Earth's magnetic field to aim their pounce at prey hidden under snow, studies suggest, often facing north-east.
Backyard and garden critters by weight.European badger: Badgers' underground setts are passed down for generations, with dozens of tunnels and chambers, and are kept stocked with fresh grass bedding.

Dewey Decimal classes, from the first sh.General works: It includes encyclopedias and computer science, a catch-all category for things that fit no single subject. Melvil Dewey created the system in 1876.
Dewey Decimal classes, from the first sh.Philosophy & psychology: Covers the study of mind and thinking. Its numbers are used for subjects like ethics and logic.
Dewey Decimal classes, from the first sh.Religion: The class gives most of its space to Christianity, a feature often criticized as biased.
Dewey Decimal classes, from the first sh.Social sciences: Covers law, education, politics and economics.
Dewey Decimal classes, from the first sh.Language: Linguistics lives here, while the literature of each language is kept in the 800s.
Dewey Decimal classes, from the first sh.Science: Mathematics sits at 510 and has its own shelf, with astronomy, physics and biology nearby.
Dewey Decimal classes, from the first sh.Technology: Despite the name, it also holds medicine and even cooking.
Dewey Decimal classes, from the first sh.Arts & recreation: Sport and music live here as well as painting and architecture.
Dewey Decimal classes, from the first sh.Literature: Poetry, plays and criticism are shelved by language, so English literature is at 820.
Dewey Decimal classes, from the first sh.History & geography: Travel guides and biography often land here, with histories sorted by country.

A brief history of the toilet.Mohenjo-daro's toilets: Archaeologists found sophisticated drains and bathrooms in Indus Valley cities such as Mohenjo-daro, with flush-like systems.
A brief history of the toilet.Toilet paper noted in China: A Chinese scholar, Yan Zhitui, wrote of using paper in the toilet, centuries before it reached the West.
A brief history of the toilet.Harington's flush toilet: Queen Elizabeth I's godson, Sir John Harington, designed a flushing toilet with a cistern, and she reportedly had one.
A brief history of the toilet.The bidet: The French bidet, whose name means 'pony', was invented as a washing bowl for the aristocracy.
A brief history of the toilet.S-bend pipe patented: Alexander Cumming's S-bend, a curved pipe trapping water, blocked sewer smells, a key advance for sanitation.
A brief history of the toilet.Gayetty's toilet paper: Joseph Gayetty sold the first commercially packaged toilet paper in the US, printing his name on every sheet.
A brief history of the toilet.Toilet roll patented: Seth Wheeler patented perforated rolled toilet paper, and the idea became a fixture in bathrooms around the world.
A brief history of the toilet.'Splinter-free' toilet paper: Northern Tissue boasted of its 'splinter-free' paper in 1935, a reminder that earlier toilet paper really could contain wood bits.
A brief history of the toilet.TOTO Washlet: Japan's TOTO launched the Washlet, a toilet seat with a built-in bidet, and it's now standard in many homes.
A brief history of the toilet.World Toilet Day: The UN designated World Toilet Day to draw attention to the billions who lack safe sanitation, and it falls on 19 November.

When these historical figures died.Christopher Columbus: Columbus died in Spain in 1506, still insisting he had reached Asia, and he was never fully recognized as the discoverer of a new continent.
When these historical figures died.Henry VIII: He had six wives, and his break with the Pope to marry Anne Boleyn created the Church of England, which still exists today.
When these historical figures died.Elizabeth I: Her 44-year reign gave the Elizabethan era its name, and she never married, which earned her the title of the Virgin Queen.
When these historical figures died.Galileo Galilei: The astronomer spent his last years under house arrest for defending a Sun-centered universe, and Isaac Newton was born the same year.
When these historical figures died.Louis XIV: The Sun King ruled France for 72 years, the longest verified reign of any monarch in European history, and he built Versailles.
When these historical figures died.George Washington: The first US president died at Mount Vernon, and his will freed the people he enslaved after the death of his wife Martha.
When these historical figures died.Napoleon Bonaparte: The emperor died in exile on the remote island of St Helena in the South Atlantic, and theories of arsenic poisoning persist.
When these historical figures died.Abraham Lincoln: Assassinated at Ford's Theatre, he died the morning after being shot, just days after the Civil War effectively ended.
When these historical figures died.Queen Victoria: Her 63-year reign was the longest of any British monarch until Elizabeth II surpassed it in 2015, and an entire era carries her name.
When these historical figures died.Winston Churchill: The wartime prime minister received a state funeral, and had won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1953 for his histories and speeches.

iPhone features, by when they debuted.App Store: It launched with about 500 apps; the first iPhone had no apps from outside developers at all.
iPhone features, by when they debuted.Video recording: Earlier iPhones couldn't shoot video; the 3GS added it, along with voice control and a built-in compass.
iPhone features, by when they debuted.Retina display: Apple called it 'Retina' because at normal viewing distance its pixels were meant to be too small to tell apart.
iPhone features, by when they debuted.Siri: Siri began as a separate app that Apple bought, and debuted as a beta feature on this phone.
iPhone features, by when they debuted.Lightning port: The small reversible connector replaced the wide 30-pin dock port used since the iPod.
iPhone features, by when they debuted.Touch ID: A fingerprint sensor in the home button, it made unlocking quick and later enabled payments and app purchases.
iPhone features, by when they debuted.Apple Pay: It used NFC and tokenized card numbers, so shops never see your real card number.
iPhone features, by when they debuted.No headphone jack: Apple removed the jack and bundled an adapter, a controversial move that other phone makers soon copied.
iPhone features, by when they debuted.Face ID: It maps your face using thousands of infrared dots, and it replaced the home button on this model.
iPhone features, by when they debuted.USB-C port: EU common-charger rules pushed Apple to swap Lightning for this standard, ending an 11-year run.

How long it takes, inside your body.One eye blink: A blink is so fast that your brain edits out the brief darkness; people blink roughly 15 times a minute.
How long it takes, inside your body.One resting heartbeat: Over a lifetime a heart beats roughly two and a half billion times without a break.
How long it takes, inside your body.One resting breath: You take around 20,000 breaths a day, usually without noticing; the rhythm is set by the brainstem.
How long it takes, inside your body.Blood's full lap of the body: At rest the heart pumps about five litres a minute, so blood laps the whole body in roughly a minute.
How long it takes, inside your body.Stomach empties a meal: Stomach acid is strong enough to dissolve some metals, yet the stomach lining renews itself every few days.
How long it takes, inside your body.Food's trip through the gut: Meals spend hours in the stomach and small intestine and then a day or more in the colon, so timing varies widely.
How long it takes, inside your body.Broken arm heals: Bones heal by first building a soft callus that later hardens; children usually mend faster than adults.
How long it takes, inside your body.Fingernail fully regrows: Fingernails grow about 3 mm a month, roughly three times faster than toenails.
How long it takes, inside your body.Full-term pregnancy: Doctors count 40 weeks from the last period, so 'full term' is a bit more than nine calendar months.
How long it takes, inside your body.Big toenail fully regrows: Toenails grow only about 1 mm a month, which is why a lost big toenail takes so long to return.

Which came first? A surprising timeline.Great Pyramid of Giza is built: It was the tallest human-made structure on Earth for roughly 3,800 years.
Which came first? A surprising timeline.Last woolly mammoths die out: Woolly mammoths survived on Wrangel Island until about 2000 BC, when the pyramids were already old.
Which came first? A surprising timeline.Cleopatra is born: She lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.
Which came first? A surprising timeline.Oxford starts teaching: It is the oldest English-speaking university, and is older than the Aztec Empire.
Which came first? A surprising timeline.Aztecs found Tenochtitlan: They founded their island capital in a lake, on the site of today's Mexico City.
Which came first? A surprising timeline.Fax machine is patented: Alexander Bain patented it decades before the telephone was invented.
Which came first? A surprising timeline.Nintendo is founded: Founded in Kyoto, it first made hanafuda playing cards.
Which came first? A surprising timeline.The Ottoman Empire ends: The sultanate was abolished in 1922, a year before Turkey became a republic.
Which came first? A surprising timeline.Sliced bread goes on sale: Chillicothe, Missouri, sold pre-sliced loaves after Otto Rohwedder's machine, inspiring the phrase 'best thing since sliced bread'.
Which came first? A surprising timeline.France's last guillotining: Hamida Djandoubi was guillotined in Marseille in 1977, the same year Star Wars premiered.

When these desserts were invented.Sachertorte: A 16-year-old apprentice, Franz Sacher, invented it for Prince Metternich, and rival Viennese hotels fought a famous legal battle over the "original".
When these desserts were invented.Boston cream pie: Despite the name, it is a cake, not a pie, and it's Massachusetts's official state dessert.
When these desserts were invented.Chocolate brownie: Said to have been created at Chicago's Palmer House hotel for the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition.
When these desserts were invented.Crêpes Suzette: Legend says a waiter set the sauce alight by accident while serving a prince, and the dessert was named for a lady at the table.
When these desserts were invented.S'mores: The first known recipe appeared in a Girl Scout handbook, and the name is short for "some more".
When these desserts were invented.Rice Krispies Treats: It was developed in the Kellogg's kitchens, and the original recipe uses marshmallows and cereal, and no baking.
When these desserts were invented.German chocolate cake: It's named after Sam German, an American baker who developed the chocolate, not after Germany.
When these desserts were invented.Banoffee pie: The name merges banana and toffee, and it was created at the Hungry Monk restaurant in Sussex, England.
When these desserts were invented.Molten lava cake: Chef Jean-Georges Vongerichten says he came up with it when a chocolate cake came out undercooked, so it flowed out when cut.
When these desserts were invented.Cronut: Pastry chef Dominique Ansel's croissant-doughnut hybrid triggered lines around the block in New York, and he trademarked the name.

Hailstone sizes, as named by forecasters.Pea: Hail forms when updrafts toss ice through layers of supercooled water, so sliced stones show onion-like rings.
Hailstone sizes, as named by forecasters.Penny: US forecasters compare hail to coins and sports balls because spotters can describe them instantly; a penny is below severe size.
Hailstone sizes, as named by forecasters.Nickel: Forecasters use everyday objects because they are quick to compare in storm spotter reports, and a nickel-sized stone is just under severe.
Hailstone sizes, as named by forecasters.Quarter: One inch is the threshold at which the US National Weather Service calls hail severe, raised from three quarters of an inch in 2010.
Hailstone sizes, as named by forecasters.Half dollar: Stones this big start to dent car roofs and damage roofing shingles.
Hailstone sizes, as named by forecasters.Golf ball: Golf-ball hail can crack windshields and fall at highway speeds.
Hailstone sizes, as named by forecasters.Hen egg: Two-inch stones fall at roughly 60 mph, enough to seriously damage roofs, cars and crops.
Hailstone sizes, as named by forecasters.Tennis ball: Hail this big can injure people and livestock, and usually comes from supercell storms with strong rotating updrafts.
Hailstone sizes, as named by forecasters.Baseball: Hail this size mostly comes from supercells, whose rotating updrafts hold ice aloft long enough to grow.
Hailstone sizes, as named by forecasters.Grapefruit: The US record stone fell at Vivian, South Dakota in 2010: eight inches across and almost two pounds.

Archbishops of Canterbury, by appointmen.Augustine: Sent by Pope Gregory the Great to convert the English, he founded the see at Canterbury; he is not Augustine of Hippo.
Archbishops of Canterbury, by appointmen.Dunstan: A skilled metalworker, he is said in legend to have seized the Devil by the nose with a pair of red-hot tongs.
Archbishops of Canterbury, by appointmen.Lanfranc: An Italian appointed by William the Conqueror, he rebuilt Canterbury Cathedral after a fire in 1067.
Archbishops of Canterbury, by appointmen.Anselm: A theologian who proposed the 'ontological argument' for God's existence, he clashed with kings over church independence.
Archbishops of Canterbury, by appointmen.Thomas Becket: He fell out with Henry II and was murdered in his cathedral in 1170, making Canterbury a pilgrimage destination.
Archbishops of Canterbury, by appointmen.Stephen Langton: He helped shape Magna Carta, and is also credited with dividing the Bible into the chapters we still use.
Archbishops of Canterbury, by appointmen.Thomas Cranmer: He wrote the Book of Common Prayer and was burned at the stake in 1556 under Mary I.
Archbishops of Canterbury, by appointmen.William Laud: A close ally of Charles I, he was tried by Parliament and beheaded in 1645.
Archbishops of Canterbury, by appointmen.William Temple: He led the Church during the Second World War and is credited with popularising the term 'welfare state'.
Archbishops of Canterbury, by appointmen.Rowan Williams: A Welsh theologian and published poet, he later became Master of Magdalene College, Cambridge.

When these ancient landmarks were destro.Temple of Artemis: Built in Ephesus, the Temple of Artemis was a Wonder of the Ancient World. Herostratus burned it down, reportedly just to become famous.
When these ancient landmarks were destro.Persepolis: Alexander's army burned the Persian ceremonial capital Persepolis. Its ruins still show grand reliefs of tribute-bearers from across the empire.
When these ancient landmarks were destro.Carthage: Carthage fell to Rome after the Third Punic War. The story that Romans sowed its fields with salt is probably a later legend.
When these ancient landmarks were destro.Serapeum of Alexandria: This temple, a sister library to Alexandria's, was wrecked when Emperor Theodosius's decrees against pagan worship stirred up Christian mobs.
When these ancient landmarks were destro.Monte Cassino Abbey: Founded by Saint Benedict around 529, this abbey was destroyed by Lombards, then rebuilt and bombed to rubble in 1944, then rebuilt again.
When these ancient landmarks were destro.Somnath Temple: Somnath on India's Gujarat coast was famously raided by Mahmud of Ghazni. It was rebuilt many times, most recently in the 20th century.
When these ancient landmarks were destro.Nalanda: Nalanda in Bihar was one of the world's earliest residential universities, hosting thousands of students from across Asia before it was sacked.
When these ancient landmarks were destro.House of Wisdom, Baghdad: Mongol forces under Hulagu Khan sacked Baghdad in 1258. Accounts say the Tigris ran dark with ink from the books thrown into it.
When these ancient landmarks were destro.Lighthouse of Alexandria: The great Pharos was among the tallest man-made structures for centuries. Earthquakes finally brought it down, and its stones went into a fort.
When these ancient landmarks were destro.Mausoleum at Halicarnassus: Its tomb gave us the word mausoleum. Earthquakes toppled it over time, and in the 1400s the Knights of St John used the stones for a castle.

France's regimes, in order.First Republic: Born after the monarchy fell, it launched a new calendar with ten-day weeks and renamed months.
France's regimes, in order.First Empire: Napoleon crowned himself emperor in 1804 at Notre-Dame, taking the crown from the pope's hands.
France's regimes, in order.Bourbon Restoration: Louis XVIII, brother of the guillotined Louis XVI, returned to the throne but accepted a charter limiting royal power.
France's regimes, in order.July Monarchy: Louis-Philippe, the 'Citizen King', came to power after the July Revolution and ruled until 1848.
France's regimes, in order.Second Republic: Its first presidential election, in 1848, chose Louis-Napoleon Bonaparte, who later made himself emperor.
France's regimes, in order.Second Empire: Napoleon III's era saw Baron Haussmann rebuild Paris with the broad boulevards the city is famous for.
France's regimes, in order.Third Republic: France's longest-lived regime since 1789, born from defeat in the Franco-Prussian War. The Eiffel Tower was built under it.
France's regimes, in order.Vichy France: Led by Marshal Pétain, it collaborated with Nazi Germany and governed from the spa town of Vichy.
France's regimes, in order.Fourth Republic: Brief and unstable, with over 20 governments in 12 years, and it collapsed over the crisis in Algeria.
France's regimes, in order.Fifth Republic: General de Gaulle's constitution created a strong presidency. It is the regime France still lives under today.

The year they would have turned 100.John F. Kennedy: Born May 29, 1917, he became the youngest elected US president, at age 43.
The year they would have turned 100.Marilyn Monroe: Born Norma Jeane Mortenson in Los Angeles. She would have turned 100 in 2026.
Born Michael King Jr.; his father renamed both of them after the German reformer Martin Luther.
The year they would have turned 100.Elvis Presley: Born January 8, 1935, in Tupelo, Mississippi. His twin brother Jesse Garon was stillborn.
The year they would have turned 100.John Lennon: Born in Liverpool in 1940 during a German air raid, he would have turned 100 in 2040.
The year they would have turned 100.Freddie Mercury: Born Farrokh Bulsara in Zanzibar, the singer's family moved to England in 1964.
The year they would have turned 100.Michael Jackson: Born in Gary, Indiana, in 1958, he joined his brothers' group the Jackson 5 as a child.
The year they would have turned 100.Princess Diana: Born Diana Spencer at Park House on the Sandringham estate in 1961.
The year they would have turned 100.Kurt Cobain: Born in Aberdeen, Washington, in 1967. Nirvana's Nevermind came out when he was 24.
The year they would have turned 100.Amy Winehouse: Born in London in 1983. Her album Back to Black won five Grammys in 2008.

How many bits these take up.One hex digit: A hex digit, half a byte, is called a nibble, and represents values from 0 to F.
How many bits these take up.Standard ASCII character: Seven bits can encode 128 characters. It was usually stored in an eight-bit byte with a spare bit.
How many bits these take up.Byte: The term was coined by Werner Buchholz in 1956, and eight bits became standard through IBM's System/360.
How many bits these take up.Unicode code point (max): The maximum Unicode code point, U+10FFFF, needs 21 bits. That leaves room for over a million characters.
How many bits these take up.IPv4 address: About 4.3 billion addresses; the pool of free ones ran out in 2011.
How many bits these take up.MAC address: Its hardware address is written as six hex pairs. The first half identifies the manufacturer.
How many bits these take up.Double-precision float: IEEE 754 doubles cannot represent 0.1 exactly, a classic source of programmers' surprises.
How many bits these take up.IPv6 address: It offers about 340 undecillion addresses, enough to give every grain of sand on Earth many of its own.
How many bits these take up.SHA-1 hash: Google demonstrated a practical collision in 2017, ending the hash's use for security.
How many bits these take up.Bitcoin block hash: It is the 256-bit SHA-256 hash; Bitcoin miners search for one with many leading zeros.

Rome's legendary founders and kings, in.Aeneas: The Trojan prince was said to have fled burning Troy, carrying his father on his back. Virgil made him Rome's ancestor in the Aeneid.
Rome's legendary founders and kings, in.Ascanius: Aeneas's son was said to have founded Alba Longa. His other name, Iulus, was claimed by the Julii, Julius Caesar's family.
Rome's legendary founders and kings, in.Romulus: Legend says he and his twin Remus were raised by a she-wolf. After killing his brother, he founded Rome in 753 BC.
Rome's legendary founders and kings, in.Numa Pompilius: This pious second king was said to have created the calendar and priesthoods. His reign was peaceful, unlike his predecessor's.
Rome's legendary founders and kings, in.Tullus Hostilius: This warlike king destroyed the city of Alba Longa and moved its people to Rome. Legend says he was killed by a lightning bolt.
Rome's legendary founders and kings, in.Ancus Marcius: Tradition credits this king with building Rome's first bridge across the Tiber, and founding its port at Ostia. He was Numa's grandson.
Rome's legendary founders and kings, in.Tarquinius Priscus: An Etruscan immigrant who became king, he is said to have begun the Circus Maximus. He was murdered by assassins sent by his predecessor's sons.
Rome's legendary founders and kings, in.Servius Tullius: He was said to have organised Rome's first census, and built the first city wall. Legend claims he was the son of a slave woman.
Rome's legendary founders and kings, in.Tarquinius Superbus: His name means "the Proud", and his tyranny led to his overthrow in 509 BC. After that, Rome swore never to have a king again.
Rome's legendary founders and kings, in.Lucius Junius Brutus: He led the revolt that drove out the last king, and became one of the first two consuls. A later Brutus, a Caesar's assassin, claimed him as an ancestor.

Bird numbers trivia.Eggs an emperor penguin lays: The male keeps the single egg on his feet through the dark Antarctic winter for about two months.
Bird numbers trivia.Toes on an ostrich's foot: It is the only bird with two toes per foot, and its large toe has a hoof-like nail.
Bird numbers trivia.Toes on a robin's foot: Three toes point forward and one backward, a typical perching bird's foot.
Bird numbers trivia.Neck bones in an owl: An owl has 14 neck vertebrae, twice as many as a human, which helps it turn its head so far.
Bird numbers trivia.Neck bones in a mute swan: Mute swans have around 24 neck bones, among the highest counts in birds, giving their long, graceful necks.
Bird numbers trivia.Hummingbird wingbeats/second: Ruby-throated hummingbirds beat at roughly 53 flaps per second, and smaller species go faster.
Bird numbers trivia.Degrees an owl can turn: Special blood-vessel adaptations keep blood flowing to the brain while the head swivels around.
Bird numbers trivia.Feathers on a hummingbird: Hummingbirds have among the fewest feathers of any bird, so tiny that each one counts.
Bird numbers trivia.Woodpecker pecks per day: Its skull cushions the impact of each strike, so it never gets a headache.
Bird numbers trivia.Feathers on a swan: A tundra swan was once counted at about 25,000 feathers, most of them on the head and neck.

Creepy-crawlies by body length.Fairyfly: Fairyflies are tiny parasitic wasps, among the smallest insects known. Some species are smaller than a single-celled amoeba, and lay eggs inside other insects' eggs.
Creepy-crawlies by body length.Flea: A flea can jump about 100 times its own body length, which would be like a person leaping over a skyscraper. It feeds on the blood of mammals and birds.
Creepy-crawlies by body length.Garden ant: Ants communicate mostly by chemical scent trails. A colony may include thousands of workers, and some ants carry loads many times their own weight.
Creepy-crawlies by body length.Housefly: Houseflies taste with their feet and beat their wings around 200 times a second. They can vomit digestive juices onto food to soften it.
Creepy-crawlies by body length.Honeybee: A honeybee beats its wings roughly 230 times a second, creating its buzz. It also uses a waggle dance to tell hive mates where flowers are.
Creepy-crawlies by body length.Bumblebee queen: Only the queen survives the winter, and in spring she founds a new nest alone. Bumblebees can warm up their flight muscles by shivering.
Creepy-crawlies by body length.Stag beetle (male): The male's huge antler-like jaws are used for wrestling rivals, not for biting. It is one of the largest beetles in Europe, and larvae live in rotting wood for years.
Creepy-crawlies by body length.Emperor dragonfly: One of the largest dragonflies in Britain and Europe, it can fly at up to about 30 km/h. Males patrol a pond, chasing off any rival.
Creepy-crawlies by body length.Goliath beetle: Among the heaviest insects on Earth, with larvae that can grow as big as a person's fist. It lives in African tropical forests and is a strong flyer.
Creepy-crawlies by body length.Giant stick insect: Stick insects blend in with twigs and can sway like a branch in the wind. Some species can reproduce without mating, and females lay eggs that look like seeds.

Fresh pasta, step by step.Heap flour on the board: Traditional Italian recipes use a mound of flour, often fine 00 type, or semolina. A classic ratio is about one egg per 100 g of flour.
Fresh pasta, step by step.Make a well in the middle: The crater holds the wet ingredients so they don't run off the board. Italians call it a fontana, or fountain.
Fresh pasta, step by step.Crack eggs into the well: Eggs give fresh pasta its richness and golden colour. Egg-free pasta from southern Italy uses just durum wheat semolina and water.
Fresh pasta, step by step.Mix with a fork: You gradually pull flour from the walls into the eggs with a fork. Working slowly keeps the well from breaking and leaking.
Fresh pasta, step by step.Knead until smooth: Kneading develops gluten, which gives pasta its chew. It usually takes about ten minutes of work to make the dough silky and elastic.
Fresh pasta, step by step.Wrap and rest the dough: Resting for about half an hour relaxes the gluten, which makes the dough far easier to roll. Wrapping it prevents it from drying out.
Fresh pasta, step by step.Roll out thin: Italian cooks roll the sheet with a long pin, or use a hand-cranked machine. Traditionally the sheet should be thin enough to see your hand through.
Fresh pasta, step by step.Cut into ribbons: Cutting the sheet gives tagliatelle or fettuccine. The pasta of Bologna is traditionally cut to a standard width, according to a tradition kept in the city.
Fresh pasta, step by step.Boil for a few minutes: Fresh pasta cooks in just two to four minutes, much faster than dried. The water should be well salted, so that the pasta is seasoned.
Fresh pasta, step by step.Toss with sauce: Pasta is usually finished in the sauce with a splash of its starchy cooking water, which helps the sauce cling to every strand.

Arctic animals, by weight.Rock ptarmigan: It changes plumage from white in winter to brown in summer, and its feathered feet act like snowshoes.
Arctic animals, by weight.Snowy owl: It hunts in daylight, unusual for an owl, and became famous as Hedwig in Harry Potter.
Arctic animals, by weight.Arctic fox: Its coat shifts from white to brown, and it can survive temperatures as low as about minus 50 Celsius.
Arctic animals, by weight.Wolverine: Despite its modest size, it can drive wolves off a kill and crush frozen bones with powerful jaws.
Arctic animals, by weight.Arctic wolf: Living where the winter sun doesn't rise for months, it hunts muskoxen and hares in packs.
Arctic animals, by weight.Reindeer: Called caribou in North America, it's the only deer in which both sexes grow antlers.
Arctic animals, by weight.Musk ox: Its underwool, qiviut, is about eight times warmer than sheep's wool, and adults form a circle with calves in the middle to face wolves.
Arctic animals, by weight.Polar bear: Its skin is black and its fur is hollow and transparent, not white; it is the largest land carnivore.
Arctic animals, by weight.Walrus: Its tusks, up to a metre long, help it haul itself onto ice, and both sexes have them.
Arctic animals, by weight.Bowhead whale: It can live over 200 years, perhaps the longest-lived mammal, and can break through thick ice with its skull.
